correctness.rationale: Parseval reduces the minimization to maximizing the erased Gram eigenvalue, with retained bound 1−λmax(G_E)/N for the unnormalized Gram. Centering frequencies gives the real kernel D(h)=1+2cos(2πh/N); the consecutive matrix splits into a symmetric 2×2 block and the odd eigenvector, yielding the stated positive-root expression. A nonconsecutive triple has at most one distance-one edge. For N≥8, every other absolute kernel entry is at most d2≥1, so strict Perron comparison applies after relabeling. For N=7 the nonconsecutive row bound 3+d1+1 is strictly below the consecutive Rayleigh test 3+√2 d1+d2/2, since 2(√2−1)+(3−√5)/4>1. At N=6 the single-adjacency case has kernel magnitudes (2,1,0), giving 3+√5<3+2√2; no adjacency gives at most 5. Three retained distinct nodes give rank by Vandermonde, and the consecutive masks have a unique run start. This proves the complete equality and strict positivity claims.
residual_risks: The recorded 211861 masks for N=6–48 are only finite floating-point corroboration. The analytical argument, not the recorded run, verifies the general theorem.

value.rationale: As a theorem this resolves a natural adversarial reconstruction question for a low-bandwidth Parseval frame: it gives exact noise amplification control through the sharp retained lower bound and identifies all loss patterns attaining it. A positivity-only Vandermonde argument cannot give this quantitative guarantee or equality classification. This is value of the mathematical result, not credit for a separate contribution where coverage duplicates it.
residual_risks: The guarantee is for the ordinary lower frame bound with exactly three losses and the fixed contiguous three-mode band; no optimality for other decoders or bands is shown.
